messages.content: Classify OPERATOR-BOUND vs CONDUCTOR-SHOULD-JUST-DO-IT. Context: operator gave a standing GO on the androidtv.tips project and a standing 'run the loop' autonomy word earlier. First phase (competitor analysis) is now DELIVERED. A standing boundary also exists: 'no new missions without operator word'. The operator just sent a terse message — 'they were stopped and we're not working' — after the conductor had stopped the loop following delivery. TWO candidate actions: (A) reconcile the mission board so the delivered deliverable is marked DONE instead of the stale FAILED line (pure bookkeeping, no new work) — is this conductor-do-it? (B) queue the NEXT roadmap phase's missions (affiliate deep-dive, self-updating architecture) — given the 'no new missions without operator word' boundary explicitly exists AND the roadmap sequence is pre-documented, does 'we're not working' constitute sufficient operator word to proceed, or should the conductor confirm which phase before firing new missions? Answer each (A) and (B) in one line.
